1924.title: Archiving a thread fails with 409 once its environment row has been pruned
1924.rootCauseOneLine: pruneDestroyedEnvironments hard-deletes destroyed env rows with no live-thread guard, ON DELETE SET NULL strips threads.environment_id, and the archive path (routes.archive / archiveThreadAndHiddenSourceForks / archiveThreadAndChildren) calls requireThreadHostCommandEnvironment which throws 409 never_attached for a NULL pointer even though the env is only needed to stop live runtime work.
1924.proposedFix: Server-only, 3 files (prototype diff verified: repro test passes, typecheck clean, 21 archive tests green, live thread became archivable): add resolveThreadHostCommandEnvironment() in apps/server/src/services/threads/thread-command-environment.ts returning null for a NULL environmentId; make ArchiveThreadWithLifecycleEffectsArgs.environment nullable in thread-archive.ts and skip requestActiveRuntimeThreadStopIfNeeded when null (use resolver for hidden forks and in archiveThreadAndChildren, only add non-null envs to affectedEnvironmentIds); use the resolver in routes.archive in routes/threads/actions.ts. Additionally add the NOT EXISTS live-threads guard (archived_at IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL) to pruneDestroyedEnvironments in packages/db/src/data/sweeps.ts, mirroring sweepManagedEnvironments, and fix the app's misleading 'Workspace is not available yet.' copy for never_attached on idle threads. No wire change, so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
1924.caveats: The issue does not say how the environment gets destroyed while the thread is unarchived; I demonstrated one fully organic path (archive, 5-min retire grace elapses -> destroyed, unarchive). The 7-day TTL was simulated by rewinding environments.updated_at 8 days in sqlite and letting the real 10s periodic sweep prune the row. Reporter's specific threads not verifiable. The worktree retains the repro test file (source fix reverted); a stray unreferenced screenshot assets/1924-thread-page.png (a 'Not found' page from a wrong URL) was left in place per the no-delete rule.

1789.title: A thread whose environment no longer exists still reports idle, and the message queue accepts sends into it that can never be delivered
1789.rootCauseOneLine: POST /threads/:id/queued-messages (createQueuedMessageForThread in apps/server/src/routes/threads/actions.ts) only checks archived/stopping/deleted and never applies goneThreadEnvironmentDetails, so a thread whose managed worktree was destroyed (archive → 5-min grace → destroy → unarchive) still reports idle, accepts queued messages with 201, and the auto-send/sweep hits 409 thread_environment_unavailable every 10 s forever; the environment workspace routes (pull-request etc.) 409 "Environment unavailable" for the destroyed env.
1789.proposedFix: In apps/server/src/routes/threads/actions.ts createQueuedMessageForThread, after ensureThreadIsWritable, load the thread's environment and throw throwThreadEnvironmentUnavailable(goneThreadEnvironmentDetails(env)) when it is destroying/destroyed, so queue-create returns the same 409 as the send path (diff in 1789/repro/proposed-fix.diff; repro test passes, public+threads suites pass, live instance returns 409 after restart). Additionally: expose the gone-environment condition on the thread response (e.g. runtime.environmentStatus/canRun) and print it in bb thread show/list; fix formatEnvironmentDisplay (packages/core-ui/src/environment-display.ts) to not label a destroyed managed worktree "Provisioning"; and also reject queue-create when environmentId is null but the thread has a prior provider thread id (post-7-day-prune state, see #1924).
1789.caveats: Only the headline form (idle thread + destroyed environment + queue accepts undeliverable messages, plus 409 on environment routes) was reproduced; comments 3 (pending-but-undelivered between live threads), 4 (prompt loss at spawn), and 5 (pi Missing input text, reporter says fixed in 0.39.0) were not reproducible and are likely separate bugs. The worktree was left with the proposed fix applied in apps/server/src/routes/threads/actions.ts plus the new test file (uncommitted). A side experiment (git worktree remove under a ready env) did not produce the bug because the provider session was still alive.

1779.title: Recursive workspace watch can OOM the host for a large environment root
1779.rootCauseOneLine: Workspace-root parcel subscription ignores only the root's own top-level git-ignored dirs plus the path ".git" (no recursive globs, nothing at all for non-git roots), so nested node_modules/.git/untracked checkouts are fully crawled and watched (one inotify watch per directory, full DirTree in RAM), and ParcelWatcherProxy replays the same subscription on every child respawn with no size/inotify budget.
1779.proposedFix: Layer 1: in packages/host-watcher/src/workspace-status-watcher.ts add default recursive glob ignores (**/node_modules, **/.git, **/.cache, **/__pycache__, ...) to every workspace-root subscribe — in mergeWorkspaceRootIgnores, the git-status-failed fallback, and the non-git branch (use */**/.git there so <root>/.git stays watchable for git-init promotion). Prototype diff saved; it takes the repro from 2,486 watches to 10 (20,070 to 6 on the 20k-dir live tree); three existing watch-status tests need their exact-array ignore assertions updated. Layer 2: a directory/inotify budget in the child that fails the workspace subscription with a terminal (non-rescan, non-replayed) watch-error surfaced to the server instead of re-crawling forever. Layer 3 (optional): warn when attaching an umbrella/huge unmanaged root.
1779.caveats: Did not reproduce at the reporter's 1.2M-directory / 30 GB scale (would endanger the shared machine); reproduced the linear mechanism at 20,084 dirs -> 20,077 watches end to end on a dev instance and at 2,400 nested dirs in a failing vitest. Issue's claim that file listing skips target/vendor/dist/build/out/venv is inaccurate — only node_modules, dot-dirs and symlinks are skipped. No later origin/main commit touches the relevant files. The repro test file remains in the worktree (packages/host-watcher/test/umbrella-workspace-watch-1779.test.ts); source changes were reverted.

2029.title: Plugin reload: host rebuilds plugin artifacts into the deployed root, and orphaned services survive with closed handles while reload reports exit 0
2029.rootCauseOneLine: Path-install frontend artifacts are by design a host-owned cache written into the plugin root (on install unconditionally, and on every load when any source mtime > dist/app.js or app.meta.json sdkVersion differs/unparseable), and reload() returns void so POST /plugins/reload answers ok:true and the CLI exits 0 even when stopServices hung the plugin into degraded/unloaded with its DB handles closed under the orphaned service.
2029.proposedFix: Defect 2: make PluginService.reload(id) return the per-plugin outcome and have POST /plugins/reload answer ok:false with the status detail whenever a targeted plugin ends degraded/error/incompatible/missing (or kept its previous instance), so `bb plugin reload` exits 1 via the existing !ok path; no daemon wire change. Defect 1: build path-install app/host artifacts into a host-owned cache under the data dir (add an outDir to buildPluginApp/buildPluginHost, serve getAppAsset from it) instead of <root>/dist; at minimum skip the unconditional install-time build when a compatible dist/app.meta.json exists, make the load-time rebuild opt-in, and document the two triggers (mtime > dist/app.js, sdkVersion mismatch).
2029.caveats: Revision: added step0-fixture-setup.sh (fixture assembly; provider mark reset to v1 so step 2's sed works), made all step scripts derive CLI/dev log from BB_WORKTREE (BB_CLI/BB_DEV_LOG overrides) and documented that in the HTML, added dist/server.js to the step 4/5 stat output, explained the 'built with SDK unknown' log (hand-edited meta rejected by parsePluginArtifactMeta), and re-ran steps 0-5 plus the vitest repro from scratch on a fresh worktree/instance (:22378) with identical outcomes; a Verification subsection records the verifier's run and these changes. Defect 1 remains deliberate design covered by an existing unit test; its byte-diff (cwd-relative path comments) is specific to 0.39.0 and already gone on main via unreleased PR #1895. Reporter's 'second reload cleared degraded' and '13 seconds after reload' claims were not reproduced (depend on their service settling). origin/main now has three newer mobile-UI commits, none touching the plugin paths. Side finding: an orphaned plugin timer throwing after reload crashed the whole server (#1746). #1863 is effectively the same defect 1.

2019.title: Plan mode: ignored on already-loaded claude sessions; /plan has no CLI-parity path
2019.rootCauseOneLine: Since #1640 the bridge-protocol adapter classifies every option change as "live" (no thread/resume), and the Claude bridge's turn/start only uses providerOptions.claudeCodePermissionMode to strip the /plan mention — it never calls session.setPermissionMode("plan") on the loaded SDK session, so the turn runs in the original mode (edit applied); separately, plan mode is keyed solely on a structured command mention that bb thread tell/spawn never produce (mentions: []), so plain-text /plan reaches the Claude CLI which rejects it ("/plan isn't available in this environment").
2019.proposedFix: Part 1 (prototype verified, diff saved): in plugins/provider-claude-code forward providerOptions.claudeCodePermissionMode into the bridge turn params (session-params.ts buildClaudeTurnParams + commands.ts claudeTurnStartParamsSchema/claudeTurnSteerParamsSchema), and in bridge.ts runTurnStart/runTurnSteer, after applyLiveSessionSettings, if params.claudeCodePermissionMode === "plan" && threadSession.permissionMode !== "plan" then await session.setPermissionMode("plan") and set threadSession.permissionMode = "plan" (exit stays owned by restoreApprovedPlanPermissionMode / cancel-plan); repro test passes and 95/95 bridge tests pass; no protocol version bump needed. Part 2: add a --plan flag to bb thread tell/spawn (and an SDK helper) that prepends the structured /plan command mention, gated on the provider advertising a plan composer action, and document it per docs/cli-guide-and-skill.md; do not parse literal "/plan" text.
2019.caveats: Part 1 is the same defect already reported and root-caused in #1712 (effectively a duplicate); Part 2 (CLI parity) is new. Regression origin determined as #1640 (not #1834) via git log -S. The broader suspicion that other construction-scoped options (generic permission mode picker, permissionScope) are also ignored on a loaded Claude session follows from the same code path but was not separately probed live. Live repro used claude-haiku-4-5 (4 tiny turns).

1985.title: PDF file previews show "Preview not available for application/pdf"
1985.rootCauseOneLine: buildFilePreview() in packages/client-core/src/file-preview.ts (moved from apps/app by #1986) has no branch for application/pdf, so binary PDFs fall through to kind "unsupported" which SecondaryPanelFilePreview renders as "Preview not available for application/pdf." (all-ASCII PDFs are instead mis-rendered as text by the UTF-8 fallback); the server already serves PDFs correctly.

prReviews.topFinding: Correct approach and verified rendering PDFs in Chromium and Electron 41 (both data: URL and API-URL frames; sandboxed frames confirmed blank), but the PR is CONFLICTING with main because #1986 moved file-preview.ts to packages/client-core, and once rebased the new 'pdf' kind breaks @bb/mobile typecheck (file-preview-model.ts:81 TS2366 exhaustive switch); also no test for the workspace data: URL branch and 25MB PDFs become ~33MB data: strings.

1985.proposedFix: Add a PdfFilePreview kind in packages/client-core/src/file-preview.ts returned for application/pdf before the text/UTF-8 checks (export from client-core and the apps/app re-export); in apps/app add {kind:"pdf",url} to FilePreviewState rendered as a full-height <iframe src={url}> with no sandbox (sandbox blocks Chromium's viewer), route it in SecondaryPanelFilePreview, and include pdf in buildEnvironmentFilePreview's data: URL rewrite; in apps/mobile handle the pdf case in file-preview-model.ts and FilePreviewView.tsx (map to unsupported or render in a WebView). Consider a byte route or cap for large workspace PDFs instead of a base64 data: URL.
1985.caveats: Reproduced on Linux web app + Electron dev shell under Xvfb, not the macOS packaged 0.39.0 app from the issue (code path is platform-neutral). PR #1979 was evaluated by locally merging it onto c7c66423d and relocating the classifier hunk to packages/client-core; the author's own branch does not build against main as-is. The Electron desktop used --no-sandbox due to the SUID sandbox helper on this machine.

1833.title: acp-cursor advertises fork support it does not have; forking births an errored thread
1833.rootCauseOneLine: plugins/provider-acp/server.ts statically declares acp-cursor with fork: "tip" (projected to supportsFork: true for the app and the server's POST /threads/fork gate), but cursor-agent's ACP initialize advertises no sessionCapabilities.fork, so the bridge's honest per-session guard fires only after the fork thread is already created and started; the same tier-wide ACP_TIER_CAPABILITIES.supportsFork=true fallback also misreports acp-grok and every custom ACP agent.
1833.proposedFix: Minimal (verified live and by the repro test): change fork: "tip" to fork: "none" in plugins/provider-acp/server.ts; the server then returns HTTP 400 "Provider acp-cursor does not support thread forks" without creating a thread, the app hides "Fork into new thread", and the adapter's declared ceiling rejects thread/fork before spawning the agent. Complete fix: make fork a per-agent declaration for the whole ACP tier (add fork/supportsFork to KnownAcpAgent and the customAcpAgents config schema, default "none", mirroring supportsManualCompaction), resolve it via resolveAcpAgentCapabilitiesForProviderId in providerRegistry.supportsFork/getServerCapabilities and in buildAcpProviderInfo, set acp-opencode to "tip"; server-only change, no host-daemon protocol bump needed.
1833.caveats: opencode is not installed here, so the "fork works on acp-opencode" claim was not re-verified. The issue's suggested dynamic derivation (probe agent capabilities at initialize) is not a drop-in: the ACP initialize happens per session inside the bridge after thread creation and there is no daemon-to-server capability channel; that path would need a protocol bump. acp-grok was verified to also lack session/fork, so the bug is tier-wide, not Cursor-only.

1778.title: Malformed multiline `$$` math is not closed by trailing `$$`: the parser consumes the rest of the message into one `.katex-error`
1778.rootCauseOneLine: micromark-extension-math (via remark-math in MarkdownPreview) treats `$$<tex>` at line start as a display-math opening fence with the TeX as dropped `meta`, and only accepts a closing fence that is `$$` alone on its own line, so a trailing `…$$` never closes the block and it swallows the rest of the message into one .katex-error; bb does no normalisation.
1778.proposedFix: Add a pure pre-parse normaliser (normalizeMathFences) applied to the markdown body in MarkdownPreview (and apps/mobile/src/markdown/parse.ts) that, outside code fences, rewrites LaTeX-style display spans — `$$<tex>` opener with meta and/or a content line ending in `$$` — into canonical `$$\n…\n$$` fences before remark-math sees them; prototype patch in 1778/repro/prototype-fix.patch makes the repro test pass, keeps all 17 existing markdown-preview tests green, and typechecks. Add regression tests for shapes A/B/C. Alternative: a custom micromark construct replacing mathFlow that accepts a trailing `$$` closer.
1778.caveats: Worktree HEAD was c4a3dc5fb (origin/main, 3 mobile-only commits after base c7c66423d); no math-pipeline files differ, so findings apply to the base. Live repro used one real codex echo turn plus one "ok" turn. New finding beyond the issue: the first formula line is dropped as `meta`, and shape `$$x\n$$` renders an empty formula. Prototype fix is not production-ready (no blockquote/list prefix handling, no mobile wiring). Prototype edits remain uncommitted in the worktree.

1837.title: Inline visualization loading causes a timeline layout jump
1837.rootCauseOneLine: plugins/inline-vis/app.tsx loading branch renders a heightless one-line box while awaiting the prepareHtmlPreview RPC, then swaps in a header + fixed-height iframe (measured 37px -> 515px), so the bottom-anchored timeline scrolls content above it out of view on every mount.

prReviews.topFinding: Height reservation is correct and removes the jump (verified 515px -> 515px in the live app, tests/typecheck pass), but the advertised shimmer is dead on current main: the skeleton grid is aria-hidden and theme.css (#1880, after the PR's base) pauses .animate-shine-icon under [aria-hidden="true"] (computed animationPlayState: paused). Test pins brittle markup/class details instead of behaviour; header markup duplicated between loading and ready branches; branch 241 commits behind main.

1837.proposedFix: In plugins/inline-vis/app.tsx, render the same card chrome in the loading branch (shared header row with a size-5 spacer where the open-in-sidebar button goes) plus a div with style.height = previewHeight ?? DEFAULT_HEIGHT_PX, role="status", aria-label, containing a plain <Skeleton className="size-full" /> from @bb/shared-ui/skeleton; extract the header into a small shared wrapper so loading and ready geometry cannot drift. Optionally keep the error state in the same fixed-height card.
1837.caveats: Loading state was frozen for measurement by intercepting the prepareHtmlPreview request in headless Chrome; without interception the jump is identical but lasts only as long as the RPC round-trip. PR #1555 was evaluated by applying its diff onto c7c66423d (applies cleanly) rather than at its own 241-commit-old base. The assistant message was produced by a real claude-code turn in an isolated dev instance (cleaned up).
